newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten counsels caution in HK home price measures.
newsitem.headline: Patten counsels caution in HK home price measures.

text.p: Colonial Governor Chris Patten on Thursday counselled Hong Kong's post-handover government not to go too far to depress soaring residential property prices.

"The thing which causes the greatest social instability, and I speak with some political experience of this, is the development of negative equity in the housing market," Patten told lawmakers during his final question period before Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
Patten said both the current and future administrations must consider the importance of investor confidence.
"Where people have mortgages which turn out after a year or so to be higher than the valuation they're getting on their property, then you get real social problems and difficulties," he said.
Soaring property prices in the territory have raised calls for further measures to curb speculation.

C.Y. Leung, a property surveyor named by future leader Tung Chee-hwa as head of a committee to map out long-term housing strategy, has completed a report on the subject but details have not been released.
